_doc: The Boot facts packs read (docs/c1f-stdlib.md). wired=true: the launcher writes it today; wired=false: a pack reads it and the launcher does not tell it yet (the to-do list for the door's cutover).

anthropic_key_set.why: told by `cliffvm run` (the Python seat has no such fact): whether the seat's environment holds a non-empty ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (told by `cliffvm run`: only the yes or no, never the key); the claude turn is refused without it unless chat_auth is login

chat_auth.why: how the claude turn authenticates and what options.background.chat_auth shows (--fact chat_auth=...): api_key (the DEFAULT: the key of the seat's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) or login (the claude CLI's own login, an explicit opt-in; it was the released constant)

agent_writes.why: whether the model may write memory (--no-agent-writes)

nerve_pause_off.why: MEMBRANE_NERVE_PAUSE=0: the kill switch for the pause route

ledger.why: the operator's ledger file path (the decisions pack writes it)

door_port.why: the port the Rust door listens on; absent = no door (set from MEMBRANE_DOOR_PORT at the cutover)

door_secret_file.why: the JWT secret file the door verifies tokens with

app_dirs.why: told by `cliffvm run` (the Python seat has no apps yet): the folders of the apps given to it, the upper layer first; the door serves an app's `ui/` files, an upper layer's file shadowing a lower one's (docs/c1f-layers.md)

ui_dir.why: the folder of the UI's files (membrane/ui)

seat_named.why: whether the person named the seat

seat_stt.why: the speech-to-text server url, else the browser listens

seat_backend.why: the model backend's url (ollama), for the model list

router_on.why: whether the router exists (the autoselect lanes are offered)

cloud_models.why: the router's cloud candidates, as rows

started.why: the seat says it has started (Boot:seat.started = now): the packs build their nodes in setters on it (fields_live.boot_started)

chat_claude_bin.why: the claude CLI's path for the bare chat's turn (packs/chat_turn.c1f); told by `cliffvm run ... --fact chat_claude_bin=<path>`; no default: unset = the message is answered with an error and nothing runs

chat_max_turns.why: the bare chat's ceiling: the CLI's --max-turns for one answer (chat_turn.c1f; default 2048 in the pack, a threshold the operator approves); told by `--fact chat_max_turns=<n>`

request_keep_s.why: ACCEPTED AND IGNORED since the garbage collection of virtual entities (docs/cliffvm.md): a door request is collected by the engine as soon as nothing holds it, nothing is kept for a while; the fact stays so a launch line that passes it does not break

memory_budget_mb.why: the memory budget of the seat in MB (native/src/host.rs `sense_memory`; NO default): the host's sensor writes Mem:host {rss, budget, level} at every tick; unset = the level is always ok and nothing is unloaded; told by `--fact memory_budget_mb=<n>`

unload_soft.why: the soft line as a fraction of memory_budget_mb (NO default): the level is `soft` from this fraction; unset = there is no soft level (below the hard line is ok); told by `--fact unload_soft=<f>`

unload_hard.why: the hard line as a fraction of memory_budget_mb (NO number of its own): the level is `hard` from this fraction; unset = the budget itself (1.0); told by `--fact unload_hard=<f>`

unload_batch.why: how many of the coldest entities one unload pass asks to leave the engine (membrane/apps/barest.c1f/unload.c1f; NO default): unset = no unloading; a pass runs at every tick while the level is not ok; told by `--fact unload_batch=<n>`

command_timeout_s.why: the time limit in seconds of a Command run that states no `timeout_s` (native/src/drivers.rs; default 120, the operator-delegated sensible default 2026-11-13): past it the process group gets SIGTERM, 2 s later SIGKILL, and the receipt is status timeout; told by `--fact command_timeout_s=<n>`

chat_turn_timeout_s.why: the time limit in seconds of one chat turn's `claude` run (chat_turn.c1f; default 21600 = 6 h in the pack, a threshold flagged for the operator): the turn is exempt from `command_timeout_s`; told by `--fact chat_turn_timeout_s=<n>`

sql_sources.why: second SQLite files to open as entities (membrane/packs/sql.c1f, native/src/sqldrv.rs): a LIST of {name, path, mode} (mode ro, the default, opens the file read-only and immutable; rw may write); each entry SEEDS `SqlSource:<name>` as if it were written by hand, and a source that already has a path is left alone; the seat's own store is refused; told by `--fact sql_sources='[{"name": "lex", "path": "/data/words.sqlite"}]'`

legacy_page.why: the lazy history import (membrane/packs/legacy_import.c1f, door_session.c1f; #1143): how many old user rows one query reads when a session imported as a header only is opened for the first time (GET /session/<sid>/message imports its messages, once, and answers). NO default: unset, an open imports nothing (the eager `Legacy:seat.import` stays); told by `--fact legacy_page=<n>`

effect_workers.why: the cap on Command / File / Fetch / SqlQuery effects running at once (native/src/store.rs `effect_limited`; default 4, operator-approved 2026-11-13): an effect past the cap waits for a slot; a held door request, an open stream and `Command.stop` are no workers; told by `--fact effect_workers=<n>`

eval_stats.why: the eval accounting (native/src/stats.rs): default ON; `--fact eval_stats=false` turns it off (no counting, no `Stats:eval` entity). On, `Stats:eval` holds the top 20 getters/setters by self time of the last window and of the lifetime

eval_stats_window_s.why: the seconds between two publications of `Stats:eval` (default 10, a threshold flagged for the operator); told by `--fact eval_stats_window_s=<s>`

operator.why: the person the page's owner cookie is minted for (door_auth.c1f; the released MEMBRANE_OPERATOR); default `owner`; told by `--fact operator=<name>`

owner_token_file.why: where `cliffvm run` wrote the owner's token (<seat_data_dir>/owner.token, mode 0600) when the seat has a door secret; chat_turn.c1f adds the Authorization header and the run's env_from only when it is set; absent on the barest seat

owner_token_ttl_s.why: how long the owner token minted at every boot lives, in seconds (native/src/owner.rs); default 2592000 (30 days), a threshold flagged for the operator; told by `--fact owner_token_ttl_s=<n>`

quota_probe_s.why: the quota probe interval the page shows, seconds (released PROBE_S 600); a `--fact` setting, default 600

map_tile_k.why: the field map's tile size `tile_k` in the empty 3D projection (released 150); a `--fact` setting, default 150

field_tau_s.why: the field current's fade `tau_s` / options `current_tau_s`, seconds (released 180.0); a `--fact` setting, default 180.0

self_cpu_share_default.why: the `self_cpu_share` option's default (released 0.5); a `--fact` setting, default 0.5

code_runs_keep_default.why: the `code_runs_keep` option's default (released 30); a `--fact` setting, default 30

ui_views.why: which renderer owns each view of the page, a JSON dict `{"chat": "legacy" | "pack"}` (--fact; default legacy for every view): GET /ui/fieldvm reports it as `views`, the bare page mounts the chat view pack (apps/barest.c1f/chat_view.c1f) when it says pack; the page URL `?ui=pack` / `?ui=legacy` overrides it

chat_page_size.why: the chat view's first load and each "Load older turns": how many turns the history route is asked for (default 20, the legacy chat.js PAGE)

chat_poll_size.why: the chat view's polls: how many of the newest turns are read again (default 10, the legacy POLL)

chat_list_poll_ms.why: the chat view's poll period once every turn is finished, ms after the last answer (default 3000, the legacy LIST_MS)

chat_active_poll_ms.why: the chat view's poll period while a turn is not finished, ms; also the period the page ticks the clock (default 700, the legacy ACTIVE_MS)

chat_stick_px.why: the chat view: the log counts as "at the bottom" within this many px (default 80, the legacy stick-to-bottom distance; kept as state, the page has no scroll write yet)

chat_tool_chars.why: the chat view: a tool's input is shown cut to this many characters, with an ellipsis (default 90, the legacy short())
